entities.summary: The Federal Center of Technological Education of Minas Gerais was established in 1934, headquartered in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, with a focus on technological education for the region. This institution played a crucial role in the development of Brazil's technological sector, providing training and education to a generation of engineers and technicians. The Federal Center of Technological Education of Minas Gerais contributed to the growth of the Brazilian economy, particularly in the fields of mining, manufacturing, and infrastructure development. The institution's legacy can be seen in the numerous technological advancements and innovations that emerged from Brazil in the mid-20th century, including the development of the country's first nuclear power plant. The Federal Center of Technological Education of Minas Gerais remains an important institution in Brazil, continuing to provide education and training to students and professionals in the technological sector.
